name: Meter Scale
symbolsAndUnits: A, B: endpoint positions (m). L: positive length (m). Resolution q = 0.001 m. Range: 0–0.1 m.
assumptionsAndLimits: Resolution: 1 mm. Each endpoint is modeled as rounded within ±0.5 mm, uniformly distributed. Length standard uncertainty = √2 × 1 mm / √12. Alignment and parallax are discussed but not randomized.
apparatus: Metric ruler with 1 mm divisions; movable metal block; two endpoint markers.
procedure:
1. Position the block on the ruler.
2. Align A and B to its endpoints using the handles or precise inputs.
3. Read B − A before revealing the answer.
4. Record several independent placements. Pinch zoom changes only the view.
referenceExample: Example: A = 12 mm, B = 66 mm → L = 54 mm. Standard uncertainty from two rounded endpoints is 0.408 mm.
dataset: Analytic or bounded numerical model; no observational dataset implied
visualAssets: Original shaded procedural apparatus and studio vignette

name: Vernier Caliper
symbolsAndUnits: M: main-scale contribution (m). n: vernier coincidence index, 0–9. LC = 0.0001 m. e₀: signed zero error (m). External measurements only, 0–50 mm.
assumptionsAndLimits: Least count: 0.1 mm. The ideal vernier scale has 10 divisions across 9 mm. Quantization standard uncertainty q/√12; zero calibration uncertainty is assumed negligible unless discussed separately.
apparatus: External-jaw vernier caliper; 1 mm main scale; 10 vernier divisions spanning 9 mm; ideal cylindrical object.
procedure:
1. Set the signed zero error from a closed-jaw calibration.
2. Open the external jaws.
3. Read the main scale just before the vernier zero.
4. Find the coincident vernier division.
5. Add the contributions, subtract the signed zero error, then record.
dataset: Analytic or bounded numerical model; no observational dataset implied
visualAssets: Original shaded procedural apparatus and studio vignette

name: Micrometer
symbolsAndUnits: p: pitch (0.0005 m per turn). N: 50 divisions per turn. LC: 0.00001 m. Observed x = sleeve + n LC. Corrected x = observed − e₀. Range 0–25 mm.
assumptionsAndLimits: Pitch: 0.5 mm/revolution. Divisions: 50. Least count: 0.01 mm. The sleeve and circular scale share one integer tick count. Contact deformation, backlash and temperature expansion are excluded.
apparatus: 0–25 mm micrometer; frame, anvil, spindle, sleeve, 50-division thimble and simplified ratchet; wire.
procedure:
1. Set the simulated wire thickness.
2. Drag or rotate the thimble; one revolution advances 0.5 mm.
3. Use the contact button to close gently onto the wire.
4. Read sleeve and thimble, including half-millimetre marks.
5. Subtract signed zero error and record. Force is not simulated.
referenceExample: Example: sleeve = 0.50 mm, n = 2, LC = 0.01 mm, zero error = 0 → x = 0.52 mm.
dataset: Analytic or bounded numerical model; no observational dataset implied
visualAssets: Original shaded procedural apparatus and studio vignette

name: Spherometer
symbolsAndUnits: r: centre-to-outer-leg distance (m), 10–100 mm. l = √3 r: equilateral leg-to-leg distance. h: signed sagitta (m), ±3 mm. R: signed curvature radius (m). Spherical surface assumed.
assumptionsAndLimits: Screw resolution: 0.01 mm. r is an exact defined parameter in this model. R is undefined at h = 0; a flat plane has infinite curvature radius. Uncertainty in h becomes dominant near zero.
apparatus: Three equidistant outer legs; central screw; plane reference; spherical glass surface.
procedure:
1. Select Plane reference and zero the screw.
2. Adjust the screw reading on the spherical surface.
3. Set centre-to-outer-leg distance r.
4. Compute h = screw − reference.
5. Record the signed radius. Positive h denotes a convex rise; negative h denotes a concave depression.
dataset: Analytic or bounded numerical model; no observational dataset implied
visualAssets: Original shaded procedural apparatus and studio vignette

name: Mass & Time
symbolsAndUnits: x,d: distance (m). v₀: initial speed (m/s). a: constant acceleration (m/s²). t: elapsed time (s). Average speed = x(t)/t. Weight = mg with g = 9.80665 m/s² (conventional standard gravity).
assumptionsAndLimits: Monotonic elapsed time is accumulated only while running. Navigating away or backgrounding pauses the experiment; restored sessions remain paused. Track motion follows x = v₀t + ½at² with constant positive v₀ and a ≥ 0.
apparatus: Simulated digital balance with 0.01 g resolution; ideal one-dimensional track; ball; monotonic stopwatch.
procedure:
1. Choose the defined mass parameter; the phone does not weigh anything.
2. Tare to subtract the current mass indication.
3. Set track distance, initial speed and constant acceleration.
4. Start the stopwatch and observe the ball.
5. Pause or wait for the finish, then record distance travelled / elapsed time.
referenceExample: Example: d = 0.5 m, v₀ = 0.2 m/s, a = 0.3 m/s² → t = 1.27698 s; average speed ≈ 0.39155 m/s.

name: Uncertainty
symbolsAndUnits: n: count. q: instrument resolution (same SI unit as data). s: sample standard deviation using n−1. SEM = s/√n. uᵢ = q/√12. u꜀: combined standard uncertainty, coverage factor k = 1. Percentage = 100u꜀/|mean|, undefined at zero mean.
assumptionsAndLimits: Quantization is modeled as uniform in ±q/2, so uᵢ = q/√12. Combined uncertainty of the mean is √(SEM² + uᵢ²), assuming independent components. With fewer than two readings the sample spread and combined estimate are unavailable.
apparatus: Manual numerical readings or compatible saved trials; instrument resolution; independent-input propagation calculator.
procedure:
1. Select a quantity and SI unit.
2. Set the instrument resolution q.
3. Add independent readings manually or import compatible saved trials.
4. Compare sample standard deviation s with standard error s/√n.
5. Combine independent Type A and quantization components in quadrature.
6. Record the mean with its configuration.
